Classic Datil
Smoked Datil

The datil pepper has been
hiding in plain sight for 300 years.

It grows almost exclusively around St. Augustine, Florida — practically nowhere else on earth. It's a close cousin of the habanero, just as hot, but with a sweetness and fruitiness that most peppers completely lack. For some reason the rest of the hot sauce world has been ignoring it. We are not ignoring it.

"Once you taste a datil sauce, regular hot sauce starts to feel a little... one-dimensional."

— The Smoketree philosophy

We make two versions. The Classic Datil Sauce is bright, fruity, and honest — everything the pepper is, nothing it isn't. The Smoked Datil Sauce goes one step further: the peppers spend time over applewood before we even begin making the sauce. The smoke doesn't hide the datil, it deepens it. Two completely different experiences, same remarkable pepper.

Two bottles. Two personalities.

Same datil pepper at the heart of each — completely different experiences depending on which one you open.

Sauce No. 1 · Unsmoked

Classic Datil Hot Sauce

This is the datil in its most direct form. No smoke — just the pepper, vinegar, garlic, and a touch of salt, and a couple of other magic ingredients, balanced until it's exactly right. The flavor is fruity and bright, with heat that builds slowly and lingers.

If you've never had a datil sauce before, this is where to start. It goes on everything: eggs in the morning, tacos at lunch, whatever you're grilling for dinner.

The gentleman on the label — dapper hat, walking cane, smoke curling up from the earth beneath his feet — is a nod to the pepper's long, quiet history in Florida. The agave plants are a little hint of one of the secret ingredients. This sauce has a little of that same quiet confidence.
Sauce No. 2 · Applewood Smoked

Smoked Datil Hot Sauce

Before these peppers ever see a pot, they spend hours over applewood. The smoke gets into the fruit of the pepper, not just the skin — so when the sauce comes together, you're not tasting smoke added after the fact. You're tasting it woven in.

The heat is the same datil heat, but the smoke gives it a depth and savory quality that makes it something different entirely. Phenomenal on smoked meats, brisket, pulled pork, or honestly just stirred into a bowl of chili.

The skull on this label isn't trying to be scary. It's a little tongue-in-cheek — because sometimes a pepper just smolders. Same as any good thing that's been given time and heat to become something more interesting.
Our Story

Started in Fredericksburg. Fueled by one very underrated pepper.

Smoketree Hot Sauce Co. started from a trip to visit family in St Augustine. My sister knew I liked hot sauce and bought me a couple of live datil plants to take home and grow. I was hooked immediately. It's not your traditional tomato based datil sauce. It's a more traditional take on an old style. It makes such a genuinely interesting hot sauce. Not gimmicky-hot, not vinegar-dump-with-a-funny-name — something with actual complexity, a real story, a flavor worth talking about.

I started growing my own plants here in Fredericksburg from heirloom seeds from The Mayhem Brothers themselves at Save the Datil. I still get all my seeds from there. We started making small batches, first the classic sauce, then a smoked version just to see what would happen. Both turned out to be something we couldn't stop reaching for. So we decided to share them.

Every bottle is made by hand in a licensed commercial kitchen in Fredericksburg, VA, produced under VDACS permit and tested to FDA standards for acidified foods. We take the safety side of this as seriously as the flavor side — because we want you to actually eat it, not just admire it on a shelf.

We're small on purpose. Small batches means we can actually taste every run, adjust every recipe, and make sure what goes in the bottle is worth your money.
